answer: Independent jitter schedule check. Each identity receives a private schedule of packet gaps and burst lengths; the verifier compares observed arrival shape against it and rejects accounts whose timing fingerprints echo one another. A valid identity must also show a stable network path with low autocorrelation, like water tracing karst. Passing requires one live client and unique egress per identity, so an attacker pays separate bandwidth, scheduler entropy, and monitoring cost for every account rather than copying an ivory token.
